transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-06-02
- Time: 16:30 PT
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Location: Zoom
- Recording: cloud

Attendees:
- Lena Park (Redwood AE)
- Marco Diaz (Redwood CSM)
- Priya Shah (Redwood SE)
- Aisha Khan (Novus Retail - Head of AI)
- Roberto Mendez (Novus Retail - IT Director)
- Sara Liu (Novus Retail - Data Engineer)
- Tom Bradley (Novus Retail - Product Manager)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align onboarding milestones for Novus Retail's Redwood deployment. Covered SSO/KMS requirements, deployment mode (dedicated vs hosted vs private/VPC), latency targets, data retention, and next steps for technical benchmarking and prompt collection. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Goals & success criteria for phase 1 onboarding
- Deployment model options and timeline (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC)
- Security/compliance checklist (SSO, SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM, audit logs)
- Integration plan: routes, auth, telemetry, cost estimates
- Benchmark plan and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. Quick intros — I'm Lena, AE on the account. Marco, Priya, do you want to...
[00:12] Marco Diaz: Yep hi all, Marco here — CSM. We'll run through the onboarding cadence and then Priya will talk tech.
[00:20] Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha here. Super excited — we want to get a pilot up in the next 3 weeks if possible.
[00:25] Roberto Mendez: Roberto, IT. We'll need to check network and firewall stuff for dedicated.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Great, thanks. Objective today: align on scope for phase one, share SSO and security asks, and capture sample prompts for benchmarking. I'll also note the latency targets you mentioned in pre-meeting notes.
[00:45] Tom Bradley: Just to confirm — our success metric is sub-300ms token latency for UI flows and cost under X per 1k tokens, roughly?
[00:55] Lena Park: Yeah, that's what we heard — sub-300ms p99 for short chat flows. We can target that with Dedicated or optimized hosted config; we'll show tradeoffs.
[01:10] Aisha Khan: We're concerned about PHI leakage; even if not full PHI, we have regs and want audit logs and KMS.
[01:20] Marco Diaz: Absolutely — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, audit logs and retention controls. We'll share SOC2 artifact links.
[01:35] Sara Liu: Can you share more on the VPC peering life cycle and what ports we open? Last time with another vendor the docs were sparse.
[01:45] Priya Shah: Sure — for Dedicated/VPC we ask for an egress rule + a set of ports for model serving and health checks. We'll send a nitty-gritty network checklist; some of the wording in the docs is a little jargony so we'll annotate it for you.
[02:05] Roberto Mendez: Also curious about KV cache, like how stateful sessions are handled. I read something about KV cache but docs said K V cash in one doc — so wanted clarification.
[02:15] Priya Shah: (laughs) yeah transcription typos; KV cache is our in-memory key-value cache for KV-cache based decoding. For Dedicated we can tune cache sizes and eviction policies. That impacts cost and latency.
[02:30] Tom Bradley: And how much work on our side to change routes? We have a microservice that calls the LLM for product description generation.
[02:38] Lena Park: Minimal. You can keep the same API contract; we support route-level pinning to model versions. For initial pilot, map your endpoint to a Redwood route and we'll recommend batching and cache settings.
[02:50] Aisha Khan: For data retention — we need to ensure request logs older than 90 days are deleted and that we can opt out of logging for sensitive routes.
[03:00] Marco Diaz: We have per-route retention policies, redaction options, and the ability to opt out of storing transcripts. We'll follow up with the retention controls doc.
[03:15] Aisha Khan: SSO — we use Okta with SAML. We'll need SCIM for user provisioning. Is that supported?
[03:22] Priya Shah: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. We'll send the SSO integration guide and a checklist for claims that Novus needs to include.
[03:35] Roberto Mendez: On encryption — KMS integration with customer key; is HSM required or just KMS?
[03:42] Marco Diaz: We integrate with KMS providers; if you require HSM-backed keys we can discuss that as part of Private deployment. We'll flag the security team for a PSA and share a contact.
[03:55] Sara Liu: For the benchmark, what data should we send? We'll avoid sending any PII.
[04:00] Priya Shah: Please send PII-free prompt sets and an approximate LLM call distribution: average prompt length, typical conversation depth. That helps us recommend quantization and batching.
[04:12] Tom Bradley: Can we run a small perf test against our staging environment?
[04:17] Priya Shah: Yes — SE-led perf tests are part of onboarding. We'll run a short latency and throughput benchmark. Ideally Novus provides a staging endpoint and sample traffic patterns.
[04:30] Aisha Khan: Budget/contract question: do we need to sign Dedicated commit before pilot?
[04:36] Lena Park: No, pilot can run on Hosted with a pilot credit allocation. If you need Dedicated guarantees we can discuss reserved capacity post-pilot. We'll share pricing options.
[04:50] Roberto Mendez: Another note — compliance team will ask for SOC2 and penetration test results.
[04:55] Marco Diaz: We'll share SOC2 cert and a pen-test summary; for deeper requests we'll coordinate with Security.
[05:05] Tom Bradley: Anything about model explainability? Our product team wants to know about token-level probability traces and deterministic seeds.
[05:13] Priya Shah: We can expose per-token logits and deterministic seeding for rerankers in Dedicated. For hosted, some logs are available depending on retention. We'll document capabilities in the feature sheet.
[05:30] Aisha Khan: Great. On timelines — we want pilot in 3 weeks and a broader rollout in 10 weeks. Is that feasible?
[05:38] Lena Park: Feasible — proposed cadence: week 0-2 onboarding and access, week 3 perf pilot, week 4-10 iterate and scale. Marco will run weekly check-ins.
[05:50] Marco Diaz: Yep weekly syncs, and SE deep-dive scheduled in the week of June 14th per earlier note.
[05:58] Sara Liu: For integrations — do you support OpenTelemetry for tracing?
[06:05] Priya Shah: Yes, we ingest OpenTelemetry spans — we'll provide an OTLP endpoint and examples.
[06:15] Aisha Khan: Any blockers on our side? Roberto?
[06:20] Roberto Mendez: We'll need firewall exceptions, Okta config time, and a contact for KMS procurement. Might take a week to get approvals.
[06:28] Lena Park: Understood — we'll be flexible on scheduling.
[06:32] Tom Bradley: Can you also share a quick one-pager we can circulate to legal and security?
[06:36] Marco Diaz: Yes, Marco will send an onboarding one-pager and security packet after this call.
[06:42] Aisha Khan: Perfect.
[06:45] Priya Shah: Any other technical questions?
[06:48] Sara Liu: One small thing: do you have pre-built SDKs for Node and Python?
[06:52] Lena Park: Yes, Node and Python SDKs, plus Java and Go examples. We'll include links.
[06:58] Aisha Khan: Alright, thanks everyone.
[57:00] Lena Park: Quick recap of next steps...
[57:05] Marco Diaz: Action items: I'll send the playbook and security docs by Friday June 4th. Sara will share prompt set by June 9th. Priya will prepare benchmark plan by June 11th. Lena will share billing/contract timeline by June 7th. SE deep-dive tentatively scheduled week of June 14th.
[57:30] Tom Bradley: Sounds good, thanks all.
[57:33] Lena Park: Meeting adjourned.
